title: Give me more site-specific theatre- this was so cool! #Tartuffe #Andr...
transcript: Under the shield is back on the New York stage in Tartuffe. It is a new site specific production on the Upper East Side. It's called The House of the Redeemer, and it was brought over brick by brick from Italy. The show itself is performed in the library, and it really does elevate the entire evening. But coolness of the venue aside, I had never really heard of Tartuffe before this production was announced. So much so that I called it Tartuffe in a previous video and was scolded by several commenters. But it is Tartuffe. And this is actually one of two productions of Tartuffe that we are getting this fall. The other will be at the New York Theater Workshop starring Matthew Broderick later this year. And I have to say, I think this production sets the bar pretty high. It's incredibly fun. The entire show is actually told in verse, meaning that every other line rhymes. And there's a lot of comedy mind from that concept. Like they might pronounce a word slightly incorrectly just to make the rhyme work. And it's delightful every time. And then, of course, we have our central performance by Andrea De Shields. He is 80 years old and still giving it 110%. Now I will say I don't know if this was just a first preview thing, but he was on book when I saw it, meaning that for most of his scenes, he is reading from a script. It's not something That really bothered me. I still found his performance to be electric, but just something to be aware of if that is something that bothers you. And then you have the rest of the ensemble cast, all of whom seem to be having just the best time. It features performers like Ambry Man Charlie from The Glee Project, who I was really excited to see. The entire ensemble is excellent. And because it's only a 100% audience, you are very close to the action. Now because it is general admission, I would definitely recommend getting there on the earlier side. There is a VIP ticket which does get you early entry, but I didn't do it so I can't speak to if it's worth it or not. But. But even if you're just the regular general admission, if you get there when doors open, I think you'll be able to find a great seat. It is a bit of a pain to get to being on the Upper East Side, but I do think it is worth the trip out if you can make it.
classificationReason: Review of a site-specific production of Tartuffe starring André De Shields, but this show is not on the provided list
reasoning: The reviewer clearly recommends the show despite some caveats, calling it 'incredibly fun' and saying it 'sets the bar pretty high.' They acknowledge minor issues like the lead being on book but emphasize the positives throughout.
